title: Keeping a conversation going
cando: ask follow-up questions, make suggestions and talk about your experiences

about.text: This is the last lesson of Level 2. You join a community group, and you keep a conversation going with new people. You also suggest a new activity for the group.
goals: Start a chat with someone new, and introduce yourself.
Ask about experiences: Have you ever…? I've never…
Keep a conversation going: Really? What happened next? What do you mean?
Use everyday two-part verbs: look after, put off, take up.
Read a notice for new members, and write a reply with a suggestion.

chapters.title: At a community group
chapters.text:
This is the last lesson of Level 2. It is about talking with people you don't know yet.
First, you listen to Amina. She is new in her area, and she goes to a community group.
A member, Kwame, starts a chat. He asks questions, and he really listens.
When Amina tells a story, he says: Really? What happened next?
When Amina doesn't understand, she asks: What do you mean?
At the end, Kwame makes a suggestion: How about the cycling group?
After How about, use a noun, or a verb with -ing. How about a walk? How about meeting on Sunday?

chapters.title: Have you ever…? and two-part verbs
chapters.text:
There are two grammar points in this lesson.
One: Have you ever…? It asks about your whole life, up to now. Have you ever been to Scotland?
Answer: Yes, I have. Or: No, I've never been there.
Then ask for the details with the past simple. When did you go? What was it like?
Two: verbs with a small word after them. Look after means take care of. Put off means move to later. Take up means start a new activity.
With it, the small word goes last: put it off, take it up.

chapters.title: A notice for new members
chapters.text:
Next, you read a notice from the Riverside Community Group. It is for new members.
It says what the group does, when the teams meet, and how to take part.
Then you write a reply. Say who you are, and why you want to join.
Then make one suggestion for a new activity or an event.

chapters.title: Your first meeting
chapters.text:
In the task, you go to your first meeting. A member comes to say hello.
Introduce yourself, and keep the conversation going for three minutes.
Ask questions, and react to the answers: Really? That's interesting!
Ask one question with Have you ever…? At the end, suggest an activity.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a story or an article about people who meet in a group.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.
After this lesson comes the A2 review and check. Then you are ready for Level 3.

warmup.prompt: You go to a new group, and you don't know anyone. What do you do first?
choices: wait for someone to talk to me
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Starting a chat is hard for many people. One easy question helps: Is this your first time here?

conversation.title: A new face at the group
conversation.setting: It is Saturday morning at the Riverside Community Centre. Amina is at the community group for the first time. A member, Kwame, starts to chat with her.
lines: Hi, I'm Kwame. Is this your first time here?
Yes, it is. I'm Amina. I moved here in June, so I don't know many people.
Welcome! How did you find out about the group?
It's a funny story. Last month I took up cycling. On my first ride, my bike broke.
A stranger stopped and fixed it. Then she mentioned this group. Her name's Lena.
Lena! She's one of our members. Have you ever been in a group like this?
No, I've never joined one. I put it off for weeks. I was nervous!
Well, you're here now! We have lots of activities. We look after the river path, for example.
Sorry, what do you mean? How do you look after a path?
We pick up rubbish and plant flowers. We volunteer there once a month.
That sounds nice, but I work most Saturdays.
OK. How about the cycling group, then? It meets on Wednesday evenings.
Really? That's perfect. And my bike works now!

questions.q: What happened on Amina's first bike ride?
questions.why: Amina says: On my first ride, my bike broke.

questions.q: What does the group do on the river path?
questions.a: They pick up rubbish and plant flowers.
questions.why: Kwame says: We pick up rubbish and plant flowers.

questions.q: What does Kwame suggest at the end?
questions.a: the cycling group on Wednesday evenings
wrong: a new bike from a shop
questions.why: Kwame says: How about the cycling group, then? It meets on Wednesday evenings.

Making a suggestion, with a verb and -ing.

items.meaning: To talk about something quickly, and not say much about it.
items.example: She mentioned a new café near the station.

items.meaning: To say what a person, a place or a thing is like.
items.example: Can you describe the man you saw?

items.meaning: To answer, or to do something because of what someone said.
items.example: I sent an email on Monday, but nobody has responded.

items.meaning: To start talking when another person is still talking.
items.example: Sorry to interrupt, but your taxi is here.

items.meaning: Something you say or write about a person or a thing.
items.example: Thanks for your comment. That's a good point.

items.meaning: An idea that you give to other people. They can say yes or no to it.
items.example: Can I make a suggestion? Let's meet on Sunday.

items.meaning: One of the things that you can choose.
items.example: You have two options: the bus or the train.

items.meaning: The thing that people talk or write about.
items.example: The weather is an easy topic with a stranger.

items.meaning: The people who live in one area. Also: a group of people who share something.
items.example: Our community is small, and people help each other.

items.meaning: A person who is in a group, a club or a team.
items.example: She's a member of the running club.

items.meaning: Something you do for fun or to learn, often with other people.
items.example: The centre has activities for adults every evening.

items.meaning: To offer to do a job, often for no money.
items.example: I volunteer at the library on Saturday mornings.

items.meaning: A person that you don't know.
items.example: A stranger helped me with my heavy bags.

items.meaning: To talk in a friendly way about everyday things.
items.example: We chatted about our weekend over a coffee.

sound.title: put it OFF: the small word is strong
sound.explain: In a two-part verb, the small word at the end is strong. Say put it OFF and take it UP. The word it in the middle is quiet. Listen, then say each group.
groups: put it off · take it up · give it up
look after · find out · pick up
lines: I put it off for weeks.
Last month I took up cycling.
We look after the river path.

Lena! She's one of our members. Have you ever been in a group like this?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Two are about experience. Three use a verb with a small word after it.
examples: Have you ever been in a group like this?
Last month I took up cycling.
I put it off for weeks.
We look after the river path.
spot.question: Which two sentences are about your whole life, with no time? Which verbs have a small word after them, and what do they mean?
spot.answer: Have you ever been…? and I've never joined… are about your whole life, so there is no time word. Took up means started a new activity. Put it off means moved it to later. Look after means take care of.

rules.title: Have you ever…? I've never…
rule: Your life up to now, with no time: Have you ever been to Scotland?
Answer: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. / No, I've never been there.
have + the past form: been, done, seen, tried, met, taken.
Ask for the details with the past simple: When did you go? What was it like?
With a time, use the past simple: I went there last year.
rules.mistake: Not: Have you ever went to Scotland? Say: Have you ever been to Scotland?

rules.title: Two-part verbs: look after, put off, take up
rule: look after: take care of. I look after my neighbour's cat.
put off: move to a later time. We put off the meeting until Friday.
take up: start a new activity. I took up running last year.
With it or them, put it in the middle: put it off, take it up.
look after does not split: look after it. Not: look it after.
rules.mistake: Not: I put off it. Say: I put it off.

practice.q: Have you ever ___ to a music festival?
practice.why: Have you ever + the past form: been.
I have never + the past form: I have never tried.

practice.q: Have you ever met a famous person? — Yes, I ___ .
practice.why: Answer Have you ever…? with Yes, I have.

practice.q: I went to Edinburgh ___ . It was great.
practice.why: A time in the past: the past simple, went … last year.

practice.q: I've ___ this film before. Let's watch a different one.
practice.why: have + the past form: I've seen.

practice.q: Can you ___ my plants while I'm on holiday?
practice.why: Look after means take care of.

practice.q: The meeting is on Friday now. We ___ it off.
practice.why: Put off means move to a later time: we put it off.

practice.q: I'd like to ___ a new hobby, like painting.
practice.why: Take up means start a new activity.

practice.q: I've got a dentist appointment next week, but I want to put ___ .
practice.why: With it, it goes in the middle: put it off.

practice.q: Ana took ___ yoga last year, and she loves it.
practice.why: Take up: start a new activity.

yourTurn.prompt: You meet someone new at a group. Write three questions to keep the chat going. Use Have you ever…?, a follow-up question and How about…?
yourTurn.model: Have you ever lived abroad? Really? What was it like? How about coming to the Friday film night with me?

text.title: Welcome, new members!
text.body:
PRACTICE NOTICE: this group is not real.

RIVERSIDE COMMUNITY GROUP
Welcome, new members!

WHO WE ARE
We are about forty neighbours from many different countries. Nobody is paid. Everybody volunteers.

WHAT WE DO
Garden team: looks after the river path. First Saturday of the month, 10 am.
Cycling group: short, easy rides. Wednesdays, 6:30 pm.
Welcome team: contacts every new neighbour in their first month.

OUR BIG EVENT
Every September we have a food festival. Members cook dishes from home and celebrate their traditions.
Last year there was food from fourteen countries!

HOW TO TAKE PART
Come to any meeting. You don't have to be a member first.
At your first activity, you work with a partner, so you are never alone.
Can't come on Saturdays? There's an alternative: the garden team also meets on the first Sunday of the month.
Every new member gets a small welcome gift.

GOT AN IDEA?
We want good relationships between neighbours. Tell us your ideas for a new activity or event.
Contact Lena at the community centre desk, Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm.

gist.a: people who want to join the group
wrong: people who are looking for a job
people who want to sell food
gist.why: The notice says: Welcome, new members! It tells you how to take part.

gist.q: What kind of group is it?
wrong: a sports club with paid coaches
gist.why: It says: We are about forty neighbours. Nobody is paid. Everybody volunteers.

detail.q: When does the cycling group meet?
detail.why: The notice says: Cycling group … Wednesdays, 6:30 pm.

detail.q: You can't come on Saturdays. When else does the garden team meet?
detail.a: on the first Sunday of the month
detail.why: The alternative: the garden team also meets on the first Sunday of the month.

detail.q: What do members do at the food festival?
detail.a: They cook dishes from home and celebrate their traditions.
wrong: They sell food to make money.
They learn to cook from a chef.
detail.why: The notice says: Members cook dishes from home and celebrate their traditions.

detail.q: What must you do before you come to your first meeting?
detail.why: Come to any meeting. You don't have to be a member first, and the group gives you a partner.

items.meaning: A person you work with or do an activity with. Also: the person you live with, like a husband or a wife.
items.example: In the garden team, everyone works with a partner.

items.meaning: Another thing you can choose, when the first thing is not possible.
items.example: The bridge is closed, but there's an alternative: the ferry.

items.meaning: A special time, often a few days, with music, food or other events.
items.example: There's a music festival in the park every summer.

items.meaning: To do something special on an important day or after good news.
items.example: We celebrated my new job with a meal.

items.meaning: Something that a family or a group of people have done for a long time.
items.example: In my family, it's a tradition to eat together on Fridays.

items.meaning: Something that you give to a person. Another word for a present.
items.example: Every new member gets a small gift: a mug.

items.meaning: To call, email or write to someone.
items.example: Please contact me if you have any questions.

items.meaning: Something planned that happens, like a party, a meeting or a festival.
items.example: The next event is a picnic in June.

items.meaning: To do an activity or an event with other people.
items.example: Everyone can take part in the food festival.

items.meaning: How two people or two groups feel and act with each other.
items.example: I have a good relationship with my neighbours.

model.title: A reply with a suggestion
model.body:
Hi Lena,
I read the notice for new members, and I'd like to join the group.
I'm Carlos. I moved to Riverside in March, and I work in a restaurant kitchen.
I've never volunteered before, but I'd love to take part.
I have a suggestion for an event. How about a cooking class before the food festival?
I can teach two or three dishes from Colombia.
Best wishes,
Carlos

write.task: Write a reply to the Riverside Community Group. Say who you are and why you want to join. Then make one suggestion for an activity or an event, with How about…?
write.starter: Hi Lena, I read the notice for new members, and …
checklist: I said who I am and why I want to join.
I wrote about my experience: I've never… or I have…
I made one suggestion with How about…?
I wrote a greeting at the start and my name at the end.

card.title: Your first meeting
card.situation: It's your first meeting at the Riverside Community Group. A member, Omar, comes to say hello. You want to meet people and find an activity for you.
card.goal: Introduce yourself. Keep the conversation going for three minutes: ask questions and react to the answers. Then suggest an activity with How about…?

phrases: Hi, I'm … . It's my first time here.
That sounds great. I'd love to take part.
prepare.notes: Write three things about you: your job, where you live and one hobby. Then write two questions with Have you ever…?, and one idea for a new activity.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is Omar, a group member. Chat for three minutes. Ask questions, answer his questions and react: Really? Then suggest an activity. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are Omar, a member of a community group. It is my first meeting. Chat with me for three minutes. Ask me about my life and my hobbies. Tell me one short story, and wait for my questions. At the end, listen to my idea for an activity. Use simple English.

model.title: A chat at the first meeting
lines: Hi, I'm Omar. I don't think we've met. Are you new?
Yes, I'm Mei. It's my first time here. I live on Park Road.
Welcome! What do you do, Mei?
I'm a bus driver, so I start work very early. And you?
I'm a chef. Have you ever cooked for a hundred people?
Yes, at the food festival last year. And then the oven stopped working!
The café next door helped us. We cooked everything there.
What a story! I'd like to take part this year.
Great. Is there an activity you'd like to do?
Well, how about a walking group on Sunday mornings?
What do you mean? Just walking together?
Yes, a short walk by the river, then a coffee. It's a good way to meet people.
compare: Did you introduce yourself: your name, where you live, your job?
Did you ask Have you ever…? and answer with Yes, I have or I've never…?
Did you react and ask for more: Really? What happened next?
Did you suggest an activity with How about…?

canDo: I can introduce myself to a group and start a chat.
I can ask and answer about experiences: Have you ever…? I've never…
I can keep a conversation going with follow-up questions.
I can use everyday two-part verbs: look after, put off, take up.
I can make a suggestion, when I speak and when I write.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Who are the people? How do you think they know each other?
reading.talk: Do the people in the book become friends? Have you ever joined a group or a club? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.why: Have you ever + the past form: tried.

quiz.q: Have you been to Rome? — No, I ___ been there.
quiz.why: I have never + the past form: I have never been.

quiz.q: Your colleague is telling you an exciting story. How do you ask for more?
quiz.why: What happened next? asks for more of the story.

quiz.q: You don't understand what someone said. What do you say?
quiz.why: What do you mean? asks someone to explain.

quiz.q: I can't come on Monday. Can we ___ the meeting off until Thursday?
quiz.why: Put off means move to a later time.

quiz.q: My neighbour ___ my cat when I'm away.
quiz.why: Look after means take care of.

quiz.q: Can I make a ___ ? How about a picnic in June?
quiz.why: A suggestion is an idea you give to other people.
yet goes at the end of a no sentence: not finished yet.

quiz.q: How long have you ___ here? — Since 2020.
quiz.why: How long have you + the past form: How long have you lived here?

quiz.q: I ___ my cousin on Saturday. We've got tickets for a match.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the community group chat in pairs. Then change the story: a lost phone, a new job, a trip. The listener must ask two follow-up questions.
Day 2: a Have you ever…? survey. Learners ask the class, then report back with the past simple for the details. Then a round with look after, put off and take up.
Day 3: the task. You are Omar, a group member. Each learner introduces themselves, keeps the chat going for three minutes and suggests an activity. Time each chat.
Day 4: talk about the book and answer questions. Then look back at Level 2: each learner says three things they can do now in English.
